steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree and completion of project management education hours—no prior work experience needed. This makes CAPM ideal for career changers and early-stage professionals across Biloxi's defense, maritime, hospitality, and healthcare sectors seeking their first credential.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot camp. Our intensive format covers the PMBOK Guide framework and real-world scenarios, delivered entirely online so you can balance training with your current role while preparing for certification.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Register with the Project Management Institute and pay the exam fee directly to PMI. Our team provides guidance through each step, ensuring your application meets all requirements before you sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your CAPM Credential
steps_items.text: Earn professional development units across a standard three-year renewal cycle to keep your certification active. Pursue advanced training, conference attendance, or volunteer project leadership to meet ongoing PMI requirements and strengthen your competitive position.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.
